results.notes:
Built the consent-contract slice in breadth-first wave mode, with every switch off by default. Stored form and digest: the contract is stored as JSON text under `approval_contract` in task_template, not as the nested object the plan row describes, because the gateway's check_digest_stable refuses nested objects that storage would re-order. The contract digest is sha256 over the exact text bytes. The same vector is pinned in Go (contract_test.go), Rust (scheduled_contract.rs tests) and the gateway (spaces.rs), value sha256:3d4828c85b976a25447098498e5077de75aa531a0e64aebe2d68bfc8f7953d55 (cross-checked with Python).

Control binding: ScheduleCreateRequest gets ContractDigest, ContractExpiresAt and ContractsEnabled; when a contract is present the schema is sha256:space-cron-create-v2 and the payload digest appends contract_digest, contract_expires_at and contract_max_class=read. The binding travels in the signed payload digest, not as separate claims on the Decision token (decision.go is not owned). Expiry must be canonical UTC, in the future, and at most 90 days. A contract with the switch off is refused by Control and capability-core, and the gateway drops approval_contract from the template so the schedule stays draft-only.

Capability-core: VerifyScheduleCreate accepts v1 only for contract-free intents and v2 only for contract intents, so a decision cannot be moved between the two. createIntentFor parses the contract strictly, checks the window and checks every tool against capability_tools (read class, floor none, no call refinement, capability match, every matching row agrees). Non-delegable names are refused in parse and in registry verification.

Consent card: the dialog shows an empty-state note because DELEGABLE_SCHEDULE_TOOLS is an empty list until a list endpoint exists. With no tools chosen no contract is sent, so the default stays draft-only. Expiry choices are 30, 60 and 90 days.

Non-plan limits chosen here: 500 admin rules per organisation, a 200-character note, and at most 32 raw hosts in a resolve request (the golden's cap).

depth_findings.text: user_browser_site_prefs rows keyed by user_id are not erased when a user self-erases in user-core or when a member leaves the organisation; this must be closed before S6 turns the choice UI on.

A member choice does not bump the org policy revision, so S4's broker positive cache (at most 30 s) must key on the member and the choice state, or it can serve a stale decision after a member changes a choice.
Expired choices are never purged and still count toward the 200-per-member limit until the member deletes them; a sweeper or an expiry-aware count is needed.

Race: when no policy row exists yet, a member's FOR SHARE lock locks nothing, so a choice can be recorded at revision 0 while the first admin write creates revision 1; the outcome is a benign stale record, not a grant, but it should be serialised.
No audit event is emitted for pref changes; the history rows exist, but the WS06 browser_site_pref_changed event (K3-11) is still missing and is an S6 dependency.
The canonicaliser refuses IP literals and single-label names but cannot see a public name that resolves to a private address; the dial-time guard in S4/S5a and Quarry must cover that.
Owner to decide whether member choice writes should move to their own gateway scope tier rather than sharing org:settings:write:self (S6).
The Postgres DB test and the migration SQL have not been executed; the lead's harness run is the first real check of RLS, the grants and the revision lock.
Space floor (browser_entitled, migration 032) and a space_id parameter on resolve are still missing; they are S8's work and must be added before a Space run can be refused.

The internal resolve (getBrowserSitesInternal -> Service.Resolve -> Repository.Snapshot -> loadPrefsFor) applies a user's live choice with no membership check, so a member who leaves the organisation keeps their remembered read or act until expires_at (up to 90 days); close this in S4 or before the broker consumes resolve, by checking membership or removing prefs on member removal, with a test.

user_browser_site_prefs and the user_pref rows in org_browser_site_history are keyed by user_id and are not erased on user self-erasure or on leaving the organisation (only organisation hard-delete cascades); this must be closed before S6 turns the choice UI on (already in the depth register).

repository.go Snapshot's comment says the policy and prefs reads share one transaction so no write can land between them, but under READ COMMITTED each statement takes its own snapshot and the policy read takes no lock, so an admin Put can commit between them; fix by taking lockPolicy FOR SHARE first in Snapshot (or REPEATABLE READ) and add a test.

Member choice routes are /api/v1/organizations/:id/browser-sites/me[/:host] instead of the plan row's /api/v1/users/me/browser-sites; the per-org path is justified because choices are per organisation, so the plan row should be amended and S6's BFF must call the implemented paths.

The 200-per-member cap counts expired choices and nothing purges them (no expiry-aware count, no sweeper), and no unit or DB test covers an expired row still counting toward the cap (already in the depth register).
apps/Control Plane/org-core/cmd/server/main.go places the internal/browsersites import after metricsserver, out of sorted order (gofmt flags it once CRs are stripped); move it above internal/config.

Migration 023's host CHECK regex accepts an all-digit final label (for example a.123) that the Go CanonicalHost refuses, so the DB backstop is looser than the service; align the regex or document the gap.

apps/Control Plane/config/plane-service-principals.json was listed in the row but not edited; this is justified because that file contains no org-core principal entries (only Auth Core minted-token consumers), so record the decision in the plan.

results.notes: Built the org-core browser site policy store and API for WS21-S3, with no feature flag (the row's flag is blank). Routes are mounted but have no caller until S4 (broker) and S6 (BFF). Decide() is the pure decision: block wins; ceiling is the admin read/act rule (open mode with no rule gives act, otherwise none); a live member choice applies within the ceiling; otherwise ask. Source is org_block, org_cap, user_pref or default. Hosts are canonicalised to the broker golden's rules, with IP literals, single-label names, ports and wildcards refused. Writes are compare-and-set on the policy revision (409 with current_revision); every policy write and every member pref write or delete appends to org_browser_site_history (append-only by grant). Member choices are capped at 200 per org, expire at 90 days by default, and are checked against the policy revision the member read. The new migration is 023 (021 and 022 are already on disk). The gateway needs no new scope: admin writes and member writes reuse org:settings:write:self, reads use org:read:self. The only new scope is org:browser-site:read:any, pinned to the browser-broker principal. The tests in browser_sites_contract_test.go turn green only after the docker-compose shared-edit is applied. Nothing has been run against Postgres (the DB harness is the lead's); the SQL is unexecuted.
